doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

title: Bass sound, reed players and Phil Woods story
summary: Talk of bassists and reed players complaining about equipment; Rowe tells Phil Woods's story about Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: It seems like bass players are kind of usually in search for that perfect sound.

Yeah, oh man, we’re all crazy. I don’t know whether it’s the vibration — we complain more than anybody I know, except maybe reed players, they’re always ahhh. They buy a box of a hundred reeds you know, and they only use three or two. Do you play?
Oh if I’d known that I wouldn’t have said that.
No but it’s funny they do that. But I’m not one of those people.

I don’t know. I don’t agonize over — Phil Woods told a great story about how he was complaining about his horn and couldn’t get it man. And Charlie Parker came in to the club and played his horn and blew him away, and he says, “Well I’m not going to complain about my horn anymore.”
